newsitem.title: USA: US Navy sent woman photos of dead husband-lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: US Navy sent woman photos of dead husband-lawsuit.

text.p: The widow of a Navy sailor who committed suicide has sued for damages after the military mailed her grisly colour photographs and a videotape of the body of her dead husband, a newspaper reported Thursday.
Vickie Lynn Ostlund found the images so disturbing that she has suffered insomnia, depression, high blood pressure and nightmares, the Tampa Tribune reported.

Ostlund, of Sarasota, Florida, filed a lawsuit this week in U.S. District Court in Tampa and is seeking $950,000 in damages, the newspaper said. Richard Richards, the attorney who filed the lawsuit on behalf of Ostlund, declined comment.

According to the suit, Master Chief Torpedoman Roger Ostlund, 40, shot himself in the mouth in his bunk aboard the USS Phoenix in November, 1993, while it was docked at the Norfolk Naval Base in Virginia. Navy documents filed with the lawsuit said Ostlund had been diagnosed with severe depression before his assignment to the submarine, the Tribune said.
Ostlund, the mother of four children, previously filed an unsuccessful $7.6 million death claim against the Navy, saying it was responsible for her husband's death, the paper said.
